summary: An excerpt from a novel's Book 1, part 4, narrated by a high-school student who describes the school's surveillance technology and his circumvention of it. The narrator recounts that gait-recognition cameras replaced banned face-recognition cameras, that the school-issued SchoolBook laptops log keystrokes and network traffic, and that he cracked his machine to hide programs from the Board of Ed's integrity checks. He then uses a secret messenger, IMParanoid, to recruit friend Darryl to skip class and chase a clue in the alternate reality game Harajuku Fun Madness.
one_line: A teen narrator defeats his school's surveillance laptops and skips class to chase a clue in the alternate reality game Harajuku Fun Madness.
key_facts: Gait-recognition cameras were installed in the school about a year before the narrator's story, after a court ruled face-recognition cameras unconstitutional.
The narrator describes the gait-recognition cameras as having 'sheer idiocy' and believes they cannot reliably tell one person's walk from another.
The school's SchoolBook laptops log every keystroke, watch network traffic for suspicious keywords, and count every click.
The SchoolBooks were issued in the narrator's junior year, and their novelty wore off within a couple of months.
The narrator cracked his SchoolBook by downloading a DVD image, burning it, and booting the laptop while holding several keys down.
The crack installs hidden programs that survive the Board of Ed's daily remote integrity checks, and the narrator must occasionally download updates to evade new tests.
IMParanoid is the secret instant messenger the narrator uses for off-the-record discussions during class.
Darryl is already logged in to IMParanoid when the narrator messages him about the game.
Darryl says he will not skip class because if he is caught ditching a third time he will be expelled.
The narrator proposes skipping after school or during lunch and study-hall, which total two hours.
Harajuku Fun Madness is an alternate reality game (ARG) that the narrator considers the best game ever made.
In the game's story, a gang of Japanese fashion-teens discovered a miraculous healing gem at the temple in Harajuku.
In the game's story, the teens are hunted by evil monks and the Yakuza.
